Volkswagen said it would slash 50,000 additional jobs — bringing the total to 100,000 by the end of the decade, the most in automotive history — as the German firm faces cutthroat competition from Chinese carmakers. European leaders have stepped up their vows to crack down on Chinese imports despite the potential blowback: A recent poll of 1,300 German companies showed 55% back tougher trade measures against China, even if they themselves suffer . European industry has rallied together as Chinese firms target sectors Brussels considers vital to its competitiveness. All the while, competition is getting stiffer: Xiaomi, maker of some of the most advanced EVs, said it would launch European sales next year , the South China Morning Post reported. — Jeronimo Gonzalez

item.title: Data Centers Are Not the Problem
item.description:
Data centers are the largely unseen infrastructure behind modern life, powering everything from the apps on your phone and shows you stream to online shopping, banking and artificial intelligence . Inside these warehouse-sized facilities, thousands of servers store data, process digital requests and keep online services running around the clock. Most Americans may never see one, but they rely on them constantly, often without realizing it. "Data centers have been around for as long as technology has been around," Brittany Kaiser, CEO of Alpha Compute, told Fox News Digital. "Anytime you’re touching technology and using everything from social media to your email, all of that information, all of the data is being processed in a data center."
